statement: Money management is planning for the future and occasionally forgiving yesterday’s receipts.”
author: Senator John Kennedy

statement: A balanced budget is like a balanced diet—hard to maintain, easier to admire.”
author: Senator John Kennedy

statement: Voting is the only time you get to tell the future what you’d like it to try.”
author: Senator John Kennedy

statement: If democracy were a potluck, your vote is the dish you bring—don’t forget the label.”
author: Senator John Kennedy

statement: Missed opportunities are like missed buses; there’s another, but it might take a while.”
author: Senator John Kennedy

statement: A healthy democracy requires citizens who show up and occasionally bring snacks.”
author: Senator John Kennedy

statement: Voting day is the festival where ballots, not balloons, decide the decor.”
author: Senator John Kennedy

statement: If you complain about government, the least you can do is vote for a better playlist.”
author: Senator John Kennedy

statement: Elections are the democratic version of speed dating—make your choice and move on.”
author: Senator John Kennedy

statement: Your ballot is a note to the future; write it legibly.”
author: Senator John Kennedy

statement: Civic duty doesn’t wear a cape, but it does show up on Tuesday.”
author: Senator John Kennedy

statement: Democracy works best when everyone has a voice and remembers where the polling place is.”
author: Senator John Kennedy

statement: Teamwork is sharing credit and blaming the coffee for early morning decisions.”
author: Senator John Kennedy

statement: A good team argues in private and celebrates public triumphs with cake.”
author: Senator John Kennedy

statement: Relationships at work are like meetings: best when short and productive.”
author: Senator John Kennedy

statement: If you want loyalty, feed your team snacks and respect their parking spaces.”
author: Senator John Kennedy

statement: The secret to teamwork is listening—especially when someone has a better idea.”
author: Senator John Kennedy

statement: In partnerships, patience compounds interest faster than money ever could.”
author: Senator John Kennedy

statement: Trust is built with small promises kept and laughter shared over trivial mistakes.”
author: Senator John Kennedy

statement: Collaboration works when people remember they’re building something, not just owning parts.”
author: Senator John Kennedy

statement: A team that laughs together is often the one that files reports on time.”
author: Senator John Kennedy

statement: Good colleagues remind you of deadlines kindly and insult your typing gently.”
author: Senator John Kennedy
